subject: Private Host Readiness: Isolation Controls & Supplier Attestations
messages:
From: Samuel Tan <s.tan@helixhealth.com>
To: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: InfraSec Team <infra-security@helixhealth.com>, Procurement <procure@helixhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 5 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment capability questionnaire - initial ask

Aditya,

Thanks for taking our call last week. As part of Helix Health's procurement baseline for private deployments, we need a short, focused questionnaire covering: network isolation controls, supplier/software build attestations, maintenance window procedures, and operator access separation. We also need to understand timelines for a 2-week proof-of-value (PoV) in our private VPC.

Can you provide: 1) a completed control matrix (spreadsheet) mapping Redwood features to our control IDs; 2) your latest supply chain attestation; and 3) a proposed PoV runbook with operator tasks and maintenance windows. We'd like the deliverables by EOD Thursday 6/7 if possible — procurement is on a tight schedule.

Please send any clarifying questions.

Regards,
Samuel Tan
Director, Infrastructure Security
Helix Health

Attachment: helix_q1_private_deploy_baseline.xlsx (xlsx, 18KB)
From: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samuel Tan <s.tan@helixhealth.com>
Cc: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 5 Jun 2028 11:06:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment capability questionnaire - initial ask

Samuel —

Thanks for the clear ask and the spreadsheet. We're on it. Quick clarifications so we deliver aligned artifacts:

- Matrix scope: we'll map to your supplied control IDs and include references to our private deployment docs (operator roles, network diagrams).
- Supply chain attestation: we will attach our current signed attestation, plus a short note describing build provenance for the runtime artifacts used in private deployments.
- PoV runbook: we'll draft a 2-week plan focused on (a) network isolation verification, (b) operator onboarding, (c) performance baseline tests, and (d) rollback & incident playbook. We'll show a sample maintenance window cadence and recommended blackout windows for data migrations.

Deliverables: we can provide the control matrix and attestation by EOD 6/7, and the PoV runbook by 6/9. If procurement requires everything by EOD 6/7, we can compress the runbook into a concise playbook draft — please confirm preference.

Proposed PoV kickoff dates: week of 6/19 (if that works for your ops calendar). We'll include a DocuSign SOW link for a short PoV agreement once scope is finalized.

cc: Grace (Customer Ops) and Vivek (Security & Architecture) who will own the deliverables.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: none in this reply
From: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samuel Tan <s.tan@helixhealth.com>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 7 Jun 2028 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Deliverables: control matrix, attestation, PoV runbook draft

Samuel / Team —

Per Aditya's note, attached are the artifacts for Helix Health's procurement review:

1) redwood_isolation_control_matrix_v1.2.xlsx — matrix mapping Helix control IDs to Redwood capabilities, control owners, and references to runbook sections. Key highlights:
   - Network isolation: VPC-only deployment model with customer-managed routing; we provide a validated cluster-level egress-deny default and allowlist-based egress for approved agents.
   - Operator separation: three distinct operator roles (deployment admin, telemetry-read, maintenance-runner) with least-privilege RBAC and optional SSO integration.
   - Maintenance windows: recommended weekly patch window (Saturdays 0200–0600 local) with emergency patch runway and rollback playbooks included.

2) supply_chain_attestation_signed.pdf — current signed supplier attestation covering build provenance, reproducible builds for runtime components, and our 3rd-party dependency scanning cadence. Note: signed 2028-05-02; valid for 12 months.

3) pov-runbook-draft.docx — concise 2-week PoV runbook. Summary schedule: baseline collection (days 1–2), isolation verification & operator onboarding (days 3–5), throughput/latency baseline (days 6–9), resilience & rollback test (days 10–12), final handoff & lessons (day 13–14). The runbook includes operator checklists and required Helix firewall rules.

We've also added inline comments in the matrix where Helix controls map to optional Redwood features (KV caching, quantization profile lock) that affect cost/latency tradeoffs — those are noted as mitigations rather than hard requirements.

If you need the PoV runbook as a spreadsheet instead of a docx, let us know; we can flip it quickly.

Next steps we propose: 1) Procurement confirms scope and signs the short PoV SOW (DocuSign link below), 2) we schedule a 30-minute technical kickoff with Helix operator leads the week prior to PoV, 3) we run the PoV and capture findings into a final acceptance checklist.

DocuSign SOW (PoV): https://docusign.com/embedded/ABC123SOW
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/HLX-RW-2028-06

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Customer Operations Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_isolation_control_matrix_v1.2.xlsx (xlsx, 64KB); supply_chain_attestation_signed.pdf (pdf, 48KB); pov-runbook-draft.docx (docx, 28KB)
From: Samuel Tan <s.tan@helixhealth.com>
To: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: InfraSec Team <infra-security@helixhealth.com>, Procurement <procure@helixhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Jun 2028 16:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deliverables: control matrix, attestation, PoV runbook draft

Grace / Aditya —

Appreciate the fast turnaround and the detailed artifacts. A few quick follow-ups before procurement signs the PoV SOW:

1) On the isolation matrix row HC-17: can you confirm whether the egress allowlist is enforced at the node level (container runtime egress) or at the cluster egress gateway only? We need node-level denial for one of our controlled workloads.

2) For the supply_chain_attestation_signed.pdf: can you surface which build IDs correspond to the runtime image used in your PoV runbook? We need explicit image digests to match our SBOM scanning.

3) For maintenance windows: Helix runs change freeze windows monthly for clinical processing (third Thursday). Can you confirm ability to schedule PoV maintenance around those freeze windows and whether you support emergency patch application outside normal windows (we'll provide contact escalation).

If you can respond to these three items in short bullets, procurement can proceed to DocuSign. Thanks — if easier, feel free to answer inline below.
